page_hash_method: PDFs visually read from rendered pages; each hashed image is extract_image(xref) on the largest embedded bitmap of the listed page, PyMuPDF 1.26.6. A multilayer PDF can display a different polarity than an extracted component.

witnesses.description: Songjiang edition dated 1474 in the NCL catalog. The 1366 date is a recorded preface date.

pages.observation: Text cites the short title 百中經, describes ten leaves abridged to one, solar lodge degree, overlay birth hour, continue downward and wrap within column to 卯.
Left half: 子 to 亥 axis and first table half. Same column 尾三, 氐二, 軫十; chart cells separate from prose.
Right half: continuation with lodge degree cells and no repeated branch axis.

witnesses.description: Mirror description assigns to the 1474 Songjiang edition family with later repairs. Repair locus/date and exact impression are unproven.

pages.observation: Target text and handwritten heading above it; retains 百中經 attribution and prose on birth hour placement.
Left half shows matching position of the branch axis and first table half.
Right half shows the layout of the remaining table half.

witnesses.description: First-party catalog describes an early Edo manuscript formerly owned and collated by Hayashi Razan. The manuscript exemplar is unbound.

pages.observation: Right half clearly titles 日家安命法; 百中經 short citation, 下面已盡, downward counting to 卯. Left half contains branch axis and first table half including 尾三, 氐二, 軫十.
Right half copies remaining grid; left half begins 淮渦神.

witnesses.description: A later print of Chen Zhensun's Southern Song bibliographic work. Impression date and exemplar are not assigned.

pages.observation: Printed page 360, juan 12: separate Xinzai and Yizhai titles, Cao Dongye's calendar critique and compiler reservation.

witnesses.description: Archive mirror identifies Ming Qiaoshantang printing. The juan 6 imprint independently gives Wanli gengzi (1600). NPM shelfmark crosswalk remains open.

pages.observation: Juan 1 opening: Li Qin supplement, Qiaoshantang Liu Dayi imprint line, Year Stem to Month rule, Day Stem to Hour five starts and adjacent birth-month/hour life-palace procedure.
Juan 6 end: Wanli gengzi spring / Qiaoshantang Liu Longtian, and seal below the imprint.

witnesses.description: Two exposures of sampled opening leaf. Side seal and a missing corner match the Taipei sample.

pages.observation: Juan 1 opening with year/month and day/hour mappings.
Repeat view of same target spread, with matching border and characters.

witnesses.description: Same imprint text and sampled ink/seal marks as Taipei p160; digital copies not counted as separate textual votes.

pages.observation: Juan 6 last page with Gengzi/Liu Longtian imprint; ink loss above imprint and seal below corresponding with Taipei scan.

rijia.scope: Modern illustration of the printed counting directions at an observed column, not an original worked case or an absolute longitude calculation.

five_rats_crosscheck.scope: Replays the later rule; the earlier Ting Shi case only lists four pairs.

identity_scope.scope: Evidence strengthens the attested procedures and adds physical-copy or digital-source locators. Neither direct lineage from Rijia to Ziwei nor the Yuan Shao case's calculation method is established.
unresolved: Which Baizhong Jing text Tao Zongyi used, or whether it was a version beyond Chen's two titles.
The original exemplar of the early Edo manuscript and the exact edition and copy boundaries of NCL 08360 and 08361.
An independently dated earlier Five Rats procedure and the limits of applying the 1600 evidence to day-master history.
The physical-copy crosswalk among NCL 06593, NPM Pingtu 020000–020003 and NLC 2642, and distinct names Liu Dayi and Liu Longtian.
